//: CoinApp Realtime Database rules.
Design: the coin catalog is public and written ONLY by the backend using Admin
SDK credentials, which bypass these rules entirely. No browser can write it.
A user owns exactly one node of their own: /users/{uid}. They may read and
write their own counts and profile, and nothing else. No client can write a
share node, so the backend is the only thing that can hand out (or take back)
access to somebody else's collection.
THE SHARE MODEL
Sharing is a live read, not a copy. There is no snapshot of anybody's counts
anywhere: the recipient's browser subscribes directly to the owner's
/users/{owner}/owned, so the view is always the owner's current collection.
The access decision is a single grant node, keyed by READER and naming OWNERS:
/shares/{readerUid}/{ownerUid}  -> reader may read owner's /owned
Read it as "readerUid may read ownerUid's coins". The backend writes this node
when the recipient accepts an invitation, and deletes it when either side
removes the share. Because no client may write /shares, a user can never add
themselves to somebody else's list.
The three relationship nodes are all backend-only writes:
/inbox/{readerUid}/{ownerUid}   pending invite; readable only by the reader
/shares/{readerUid}/{ownerUid}  accepted grant; readable only by the reader
/outbox/{ownerUid}/{readerUid}  the owner's record, so they can revoke
Names and avatars come from /users/{uid}/profile, which each user writes for
themselves. It is readable by a reader who has either a pending invite or an
accepted grant for that uid, so an invitation can show who sent it while the
information itself is never public.
CHANGES FROM YOUR PREVIOUS RULES (3):
1. /users/{uid}/owned is now readable when a matching /shares grant exists.
This is the rule that makes live sharing possible.
2. ADDED /users/{uid}/profile, write-by-self and read-by-self, invitee or
grantee.
3. /shares is keyed by reader and readable by that reader only. It replaces the
old unreadable /shares/{id} snapshot record; there are no snapshots now.
UNCHANGED: the world-readable /coins and /meta nodes, the backend-only
/inbox and /outbox, the /users/{uid}/owned write-by-self rule, and the
newData.val() clamp that stops a count ever going negative.
